q: The 'Advice of Internal Check' in respect of a station's accounts is issued by:

options.A: The Station Master
options.B: The Traffic Accounts Office after check of the station balance sheet
options.C: The Travelling Inspector of Accounts
options.D: The Divisional Commercial Manager

e: The Advice of Internal Check is issued by the Traffic Accounts Office after it checks the station balance sheet, advising the debits and disallowances found during that check.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Gross Tonne Kilometres (GTKM) include the tare weight of the vehicles.
2. Net Tonne Kilometres (NTKM) exclude the tare weight of the vehicles.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both are true: GTKM are worked out on gross tonnage, which includes the tare weight of the vehicles, while NTKM cover only the net (paying) load and exclude tare.

q: Specific Fuel Consumption (SFC) on Indian Railways is expressed per:

options.A: 1000 NTKM
options.B: 1000 GTKM
options.C: 100 engine kilometres
options.D: 1000 train kilometres

e: Specific Fuel Consumption measures the fuel consumed per 1000 GTKM hauled, because locomotive fuel effort is related to the gross load moved, including the tare of vehicles.

q: 'Wagon turn-round' denotes the time taken:

options.A: To unload a wagon at destination
options.B: Between two successive loadings of a wagon, expressed in days
options.C: For a wagon to travel 1000 kilometres
options.D: To repair a wagon in the workshop

e: Wagon turn-round is the average time, in days, between two successive loadings of a wagon; a shorter turn-round means wagons are being utilised more intensively.

q: A debit balance under 'Traffic Suspense' broadly indicates:

options.A: Profit earned by the Traffic Department
options.B: Traffic dues/outstanding earnings yet to be recovered or adjusted
options.C: Excess cash deposited by stations
options.D: Refunds payable to passengers

e: A debit balance under Traffic Suspense represents traffic dues and outstanding earnings of stations which have yet to be recovered or finally adjusted.

q: The Travelling Inspector of Accounts (TIA) primarily functions to:

options.A: Prepare the station balance sheet
options.B: Inspect stations and prevent leakage of railway revenue
options.C: Compile the annual Appropriation Accounts
options.D: Sanction refunds of fares

e: The Travelling Inspector of Accounts inspects stations on the move, checking ticket stock, cash and accounts, mainly to prevent leakage of railway revenue.

q: Errors detected by the Traffic Accounts Office in the accounts rendered by a station are advised to the station through:

options.A: Overcharge sheet
options.B: Error sheet
options.C: Advice of Payment
options.D: Stock sheet

e: Errors detected in a station's accounts during check are advised to the station through an error sheet, so that it can accept the objection or reply to it.

q: The statement of approximate gross earnings of Indian Railways is compiled and issued every:

options.A: Day
options.B: Week
options.C: 10 days
options.D: Month

e: The statement of approximate gross earnings is compiled every ten days, giving a quick periodical watch over the trend of earnings.

q: 'Apportioned earnings' of a zonal railway mean:

options.A: Earnings collected in cash at its own stations only
options.B: Its share of earnings of through traffic, allocated on the basis of the distance carried over its system
options.C: Earnings from suburban services only
options.D: Earnings surrendered to the Railway Board

e: Apportioned earnings are a zonal railway's share of through-traffic earnings, divided among the railways traversed on the basis of the distance carried over each system.

q: The monthly Station Balance Sheet shows, among other things:

options.A: Only the cash collected during the month
options.B: The balance of traffic earnings outstanding and recoverable at the station at the end of the month
options.C: The staff position of the station
options.D: The inventory of station stores

e: The monthly Station Balance Sheet exhibits the balance of traffic earnings outstanding and recoverable at the station at the close of the month.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Wharfage is the charge levied for detention of wagons beyond the free time allowed for loading or unloading.
2. Demurrage is the charge levied for goods not removed from the station premises within the free time.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Neither is correct, as the two definitions are interchanged: demurrage is charged for detention of wagons beyond free time, and wharfage for goods not removed from station premises within the free time.

q: In Indian Railways, the abbreviation FOIS stands for:

options.A: Freight Operations Information System
options.B: Freight Outward Invoice System
options.C: Financial Operations and Information System
options.D: Freight Organisation and Inspection Service

e: FOIS stands for Freight Operations Information System, the computer system supporting freight and rake operations on Indian Railways.

q: The computerised system used for issuing unreserved tickets at stations is known as:

options.A: PRS
options.B: FOIS
options.C: UTS
options.D: TAMS

e: UTS, the Unreserved Ticketing System, is the computerised system used for issuing unreserved tickets at stations.

q: The Excess Fare Tickets (EFTs) issued by the ticket checking staff are subjected to check in the:

options.A: Commercial Branch of the Division
options.B: Traffic Accounts Office
options.C: Personnel Branch
options.D: Railway Recruitment Board

e: Excess Fare Tickets issued by ticket checking staff are checked in the Traffic Accounts Office to verify the fares and excess charges realised from passengers.

q: Tickets returned by a station as 'non-issued' are checked in the Traffic Accounts Office mainly to ensure that:

options.A: The printing of the tickets is of good quality
options.B: Such tickets were in fact not sold or issued to passengers
options.C: The ticket stock register is neatly maintained
options.D: The fare printed on them is the latest fare

e: Tickets returned as non-issued are checked to confirm they were genuinely not sold, so that no fare escapes accountal behind a non-issued return.

q: Collected tickets received from stations are checked in the Traffic Accounts Office primarily to:

options.A: Verify the handwriting of the collecting staff
options.B: Ensure that all collected tickets are duly accounted for and none is missing or unaccounted
options.C: Assess the condition of the paper used
options.D: Count the total number of passengers travelled in the year

e: Collected tickets are checked to ensure that every ticket collected from passengers is duly accounted for and none is missing or left unaccounted.

q: In traffic accounts, 'Cash-in-Transit' represents:

options.A: Cash held in the station imprest
options.B: Station earnings collected but not yet credited to the Railway's account, being in the process of remittance
options.C: Cash paid as refunds to passengers
options.D: The salary of cash office staff in transit

e: Cash-in-transit represents station earnings collected and remitted but not yet credited to the railway's bank account, the remittance still being in transit.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Outstanding balances under Traffic Suspense should be cleared within the same financial year.
2. Uncleared Traffic Suspense balances distort the earnings of the year and thereby the Operating Ratio.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both are true: Traffic Suspense balances should be cleared within the same financial year, and uncleared balances distort the earnings of the year and hence the Operating Ratio.

q: Debits and disallowances advised to a station through the Advice of Internal Check are to be taken to account by the station:

options.A: Only after the detailed error sheet is received
options.B: Only after confirmation from the Divisional Office
options.C: Whether or not the error sheet has been received
options.D: Only at the end of the financial year

e: Debits and disallowances advised through the Advice of Internal Check must be taken to account by the station whether or not the detailed error sheet has been received.

q: The Accounts Office Balance Sheet in traffic accounts is prepared:

options.A: By every station for its own transactions
options.B: In the Traffic Accounts Office, reflecting the position of station balances as per the accounts office books
options.C: By the Railway Board for all zonal railways together
options.D: By the Travelling Inspector of Accounts during inspection

e: The Accounts Office Balance Sheet is prepared in the Traffic Accounts Office from its own books, showing the position of station balances as per the accounts office records.

q: The 'average lead' of goods traffic is computed as:

options.A: Train kilometres divided by number of trains
options.B: Net Tonne Kilometres divided by tonnes carried
options.C: Gross Tonne Kilometres divided by wagon kilometres
options.D: Earnings divided by tonnes carried

e: Average lead of goods traffic = NTKM divided by tonnes carried, giving the average distance over which each tonne of goods is hauled.

q: 'Engine kilometres per engine day' is an index of:

options.A: Fuel efficiency of locomotives
options.B: Utilisation of locomotives
options.C: Utilisation of wagons
options.D: Occupation of the line

e: Engine kilometres per engine day shows how much distance each engine covers daily, so it is an index of the utilisation of locomotives.

q: Net Tonne Kilometres per wagon day is computed as:

options.A: Total NTKM divided by the number of wagons loaded
options.B: Total NTKM divided by wagon days
options.C: Total GTKM divided by wagon days
options.D: Tonnes carried divided by wagon days

e: NTKM per wagon day = total NTKM divided by wagon days, indicating the revenue-earning work obtained from each wagon per day.

q: Specific Energy Consumption (SEC) in electric traction is expressed as the electrical energy consumed per:

options.A: 100 train kilometres
options.B: 1000 NTKM
options.C: 1000 GTKM
options.D: Engine hour

e: Specific Energy Consumption in electric traction is the electrical energy consumed per 1000 GTKM hauled.

q: Tatkal charges are levied as:

options.A: A penalty for travelling without a ticket
options.B: A premium in addition to the normal fare for reservations made at short notice before the journey
options.C: A refund processing fee
options.D: A charge for change of boarding station

e: Tatkal charges are a premium levied over the normal fare for reservations booked at short notice before the journey, for confirmed accommodation under the Tatkal scheme.

q: Which of the following receipts is classified under 'sundry other earnings' of the Railways?

options.A: Passenger fares
options.B: Goods freight charges
options.C: Parcel earnings
options.D: Receipts from advertisements and catering licences

e: Receipts from advertisements and catering licences are non-traffic receipts and are classified under sundry other earnings, not under coaching or goods earnings.

q: The gross traffic earnings of a railway comprise:

options.A: Coaching earnings and goods earnings only
options.B: Coaching earnings, goods earnings and sundry other earnings
options.C: Coaching earnings and sundry earnings only
options.D: Goods earnings and parcel earnings only

e: Gross traffic earnings comprise three heads: coaching earnings, goods earnings and sundry other earnings.

q: In regard to earnings collected at a station, the correct position is that:

options.A: Petty station expenses may be met out of station earnings
options.B: Station earnings must be remitted in full and cannot be appropriated for departmental expenditure
options.C: Half the earnings may be retained by the station till the end of the month
options.D: Earnings may be adjusted against outstanding dues of the station staff

e: Station earnings must be remitted in full and cannot be appropriated for departmental expenditure; station expenses are met only through separately authorised payments.

q: The flexi fare system (dynamic pricing linked to occupancy) was introduced in:

options.A: All Mail and Express trains
options.B: Suburban train services
options.C: Rajdhani, Shatabdi and Duronto trains
options.D: Passenger (slow local) trains only

e: The flexi fare system, under which fares rise with occupancy, was introduced in the Rajdhani, Shatabdi and Duronto trains.

q: In connection with unreserved ticketing, the abbreviation JTBS stands for:

options.A: Joint Ticket Booking Service
options.B: Jansadharan Ticket Booking Sevak
options.C: Journey Ticket Booking Section
options.D: Zonal Ticket Booking Scheme

e: JTBS stands for Jansadharan Ticket Booking Sevak, the authorised agents engaged to issue unreserved tickets outside station premises.

q: An 'overcharge sheet' is prepared in the Traffic Accounts Office when:

options.A: A station has charged less freight than the amount due
options.B: Excess fare or freight has been collected from the public and the amount is to be refunded
options.C: Tickets issued by a station are found missing
options.D: A station has failed to remit its earnings in time

e: An overcharge sheet is prepared when excess fare or freight has been collected from the public, so that the excess amount can be refunded.

q: In station accounts, an 'undercharge' means:

options.A: Fare or freight charged at less than the amount actually due
options.B: Fare or freight charged in excess of the amount due
options.C: A charge which has been refunded to the passenger
options.D: A charge waived under orders of the competent authority

e: An undercharge means fare or freight has been charged at less than the amount actually due.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. 'Earnings' of a period represent the amounts that have accrued for services rendered during that period, whether actually received or not.
2. 'Revenue' represents the earnings actually realised or received.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both are true: earnings are the amounts accrued for services rendered during a period whether received or not, while revenue represents the earnings actually realised or received.

q: 'Originating earnings' of a zonal railway mean:

options.A: The total earnings of the traffic originating (booked) on that railway, before apportionment
options.B: The earnings collected in cash at its stations only
options.C: The earnings received by it from other railways on apportionment
options.D: The sundry earnings of the railway

e: Originating earnings are the total earnings on traffic originating (booked) on that railway, taken before apportionment among the railways concerned.

q: Which of the following categories of earnings is NOT apportioned among the railways?

options.A: Coaching earnings of through traffic
options.B: Goods earnings of through traffic
options.C: Sundry other earnings
options.D: Parcel earnings of through traffic

e: Sundry other earnings are not apportioned among railways; apportionment applies to through coaching, goods and parcel earnings, which are shared on the distance basis.

q: Earnings from parcels, luggage and postal (mail) traffic are classified on Indian Railways under:

options.A: Goods earnings
options.B: Sundry other earnings
options.C: Capital receipts
options.D: Other coaching earnings

e: Earnings from parcels, luggage and postal (mail) traffic are classified under other coaching earnings.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Advice of Internal Check is prepared separately for coaching accounts and for goods accounts.
2. The Advice of Internal Check is issued before the station balance sheet is received in the Traffic Accounts Office for check.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Statement 1 is true: separate Advices of Internal Check are prepared for coaching accounts and for goods accounts. Statement 2 is false: the Advice follows receipt and check of the station balance sheet.

q: The 'internal check' exercised by the Traffic Accounts Office over the accounts rendered by stations is:

options.A: A test check of a small percentage of transactions
options.B: A detailed (cent per cent) check of the accounts rendered
options.C: A check exercised by the statutory audit party
options.D: A check confined only to cash remittances

e: The internal check exercised by the Traffic Accounts Office is a detailed, cent per cent check of the accounts rendered by stations, not a mere test check.

q:
Consider the following statements about FOIS:
1. RMS stands for Rake Management System.
2. TMS stands for Terminal Management System.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both are correct: in FOIS, RMS stands for Rake Management System and TMS stands for Terminal Management System.

q: In connection with coaching operations, the abbreviation COIS stands for:

options.A: Coaching Outward Information System
options.B: Coaching Operations Information System
options.C: Central Operations and Information Section
options.D: Coaching Operations Inspection Service

e: COIS stands for Coaching Operations Information System, the information system supporting coaching operations.

q: The computer software on which the Passenger Reservation System (PRS) of Indian Railways operates is known as:

options.A: UTS
options.B: TAMS
options.C: FOIS
options.D: CONCERT

e: The Passenger Reservation System operates on the CONCERT software, the countrywide network of computerised reservation and ticketing.

q: The information systems such as PRS and FOIS of Indian Railways have been developed and are maintained by:

options.A: Centre for Railway Information Systems (CRIS)
options.B: Rail India Technical and Economic Service (RITES)
options.C: Indian Railway Catering and Tourism Corporation (IRCTC)
options.D: RailTel Corporation of India

e: Information systems such as PRS and FOIS are developed and maintained by the Centre for Railway Information Systems (CRIS).

q: In Indian Railways, the abbreviation NTES stands for:

options.A: National Ticket Enquiry Service
options.B: National Train Earnings Statement
options.C: National Train Enquiry System
options.D: Network of Ticket Examining Staff

e: NTES stands for National Train Enquiry System, which provides train running and related information to passengers.

q: Under the e-payment facility for freight, authorised freight customers pay the freight:

options.A: In cash at the goods booking office
options.B: Electronically through banks, the amount being credited directly to the railway's account
options.C: By cheque handed over to the Travelling Inspector of Accounts
options.D: By money order to the destination station

e: Under e-payment, authorised freight customers pay freight electronically through banks, and the amount is credited directly to the railway's account without cash handling at stations.

q: In Indian Railways, the abbreviation LWIS stands for:

options.A: Liberalised Wagon Investment Scheme
options.B: Long-distance Wagon Information System
options.C: Liberalised Wagon Insurance Scheme
options.D: Local Wagon Investment Scheme

e: LWIS stands for Liberalised Wagon Investment Scheme, under which customers invest in wagons for assured supply.

q: In freight marketing on Indian Railways, the abbreviation PFT stands for:

options.A: Public Freight Transport
options.B: Parcel Freight Train
options.C: Permanent Freight Terminal
options.D: Private Freight Terminal

e: PFT stands for Private Freight Terminal, a terminal set up by private parties for handling rail freight.

q: Station-to-Station (STS) rates are:

options.A: Rates applicable uniformly at all stations
options.B: Concessional freight rates notified for traffic between specified pairs of stations
options.C: Fares for suburban services
options.D: Rates for parcel traffic only

e: Station-to-Station rates are concessional freight rates notified for traffic moving between specified pairs of stations, to attract or retain that traffic.

q: Long Term Tariff Contracts (LTTC) are entered into by the Railways with:

options.A: Key freight customers who assure a minimum volume of traffic over the contract period
options.B: Catering contractors at stations
options.C: Parcel handling contractors
options.D: State Governments for suburban services

e: Long Term Tariff Contracts are entered into with key freight customers who assure a minimum volume of traffic over the contract period.

q: The NINFRIS scheme of Indian Railways is associated with:

options.A: Computerisation of station accounts
options.B: Investment in wagons by customers
options.C: Fixation of freight rates for a long period
options.D: Generation of non-fare revenue through new and innovative ideas

e: NINFRIS is the scheme for generation of non-fare revenue through new, innovative and untapped ideas and sources.

q: A Railway Receipt (RR) is:

options.A: A mere cash memo issued at the goods shed
options.B: A receipt for the goods accepted for carriage and evidence of the contract of carriage
options.C: A voucher for claiming refund of freight
options.D: A document issued only for parcel traffic

e: A Railway Receipt is the receipt issued for goods accepted for carriage and is evidence of the contract of carriage between the consignor and the railway.

q: Delivery of goods at the destination station is normally given:

options.A: To any person who asks for the goods
options.B: Only to the consignor in person
options.C: On surrender of the Railway Receipt by the consignee or his endorsee
options.D: Only after the expiry of the free time

e: Delivery of goods is given on surrender of the Railway Receipt by the consignee or his endorsee, since the receipt is the document of title to the goods.

q: Freight charges at 'owner's risk' rate are, as compared with the 'railway risk' rate:

options.A: Higher
options.B: Equal
options.C: Lower
options.D: Exactly double

e: At owner's risk the railway's liability is limited, so the owner's risk rate is lower than the railway risk rate for the same traffic.

q: Freight charges on goods traffic are determined mainly on the basis of:

options.A: The classification of the commodity and the distance over which it is carried, applied to the chargeable weight
options.B: The market value of the goods alone
options.C: The speed of the train by which the goods are carried
options.D: The number of wagons in the rake

e: Freight charges are determined mainly by the classification of the commodity and the distance of carriage, applied to the chargeable weight of the consignment.

q: 'Outstanding freight' at a station represents:

options.A: Freight already collected in cash and remitted
options.B: Freight deposited in advance by merchants
options.C: Refund of freight payable to merchants
options.D: 'To-pay' freight on goods traffic which has not yet been collected

e: Outstanding freight at a station is the 'to-pay' freight on goods traffic which has not yet been collected.

q: In goods booking, 'Paid' and 'To Pay' indicate:

options.A: Whether the freight is paid at the forwarding station or is to be collected at the destination
options.B: Whether payment is made in cash or by cheque
options.C: Whether the traffic is a full rake load or a piecemeal load
options.D: Whether the traffic is local or through traffic

e: 'Paid' indicates freight paid at the forwarding station, while 'To Pay' indicates freight to be collected at the destination station.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. A route kilometre is the length of line between two points, irrespective of the number of tracks on that length.
2. A track kilometre counts each running line separately.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both are true: a route kilometre is the length of line between two points irrespective of the number of tracks, while a track kilometre counts each running line separately.

q: 'Train kilometres' represent:

options.A: The route kilometres multiplied by the number of trains
options.B: The total engine kilometres run
options.C: The total passenger kilometres
options.D: The aggregate distance run by all trains

e: Train kilometres represent the aggregate distance run by all trains during the period.

q: 'Passenger kilometres' are computed as:

options.A: The number of passengers multiplied by the number of trains
options.B: The sum, over all passengers, of the distance travelled by each passenger
options.C: Train kilometres multiplied by the seating capacity
options.D: Passenger earnings divided by the average fare

e: Passenger kilometres are computed as the sum, over all passengers, of the distance travelled by each passenger.

q: The density of traffic on a railway (or section) is expressed as:

options.A: The number of trains run per day
options.B: Net Tonne Kilometres per wagon day
options.C: Gross Tonne Kilometres per route kilometre
options.D: Earnings per station

e: Traffic density is expressed as Gross Tonne Kilometres per route kilometre, showing the volume of traffic carried over each kilometre of line.

q: The average net load of goods trains is computed as:

options.A: Net Tonne Kilometres divided by goods train kilometres
options.B: Gross Tonne Kilometres divided by wagon kilometres
options.C: Tonnes carried divided by the number of wagons loaded
options.D: Net Tonne Kilometres divided by route kilometres

e: Average net load of goods trains = Net Tonne Kilometres divided by goods train kilometres, giving the average paying load hauled per train kilometre.

q: The percentage of empty wagon kilometres to total wagon kilometres indicates:

options.A: The wagon turn-round
options.B: The average load of wagons
options.C: The fuel efficiency of goods working
options.D: The extent of empty (unloaded) running of wagons

e: The percentage of empty wagon kilometres to total wagon kilometres indicates the extent of empty, unloaded running of wagons.

q: 'Originating passengers' on a railway are those passengers who:

options.A: Alight at stations of that railway
options.B: Commence their journey from stations on that railway
options.C: Travel by air-conditioned classes only
options.D: Are received from other railways at junctions

e: Originating passengers are those who commence their journey from stations on that railway.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Siding statements rendered by stations are checked in the Traffic Accounts Office.
2. Handling bills rendered by stations are checked in the Traffic Accounts Office.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both are true: siding statements and handling bills rendered by stations are checked in the Traffic Accounts Office.

q: Concession vouchers and concession order forms received with station accounts are checked in the Traffic Accounts Office mainly to ensure that:

options.A: The concession was granted only to persons entitled to it and under proper authority
options.B: The vouchers are printed on good quality paper
options.C: Concessions are claimed by all passengers
options.D: The highest fare has been charged in every case

e: Concession vouchers and order forms are checked mainly to ensure the concession was granted only to persons entitled to it and under proper authority.

q: The monthly evaluation report of traffic earnings is used for:

options.A: Fixation of pay of station staff
options.B: Allotment of wagons to stations
options.C: Comparing the actual earnings with the budget proportions/targets
options.D: Printing of tickets for stations

e: The monthly evaluation report of traffic earnings is used to compare actual earnings with the budget proportions and targets for the period.

q: The 'earnings budget' of a railway is:

options.A: The actual earnings of the previous year
options.B: An estimate of the earnings expected to be realised during the budget year, forming part of the Railway Budget
options.C: An estimate covering goods earnings only
options.D: A statement prepared by each station separately

e: The earnings budget is an estimate of the earnings expected to be realised during the budget year, forming part of the Railway Budget.

q: The average speed of goods trains is computed as:

options.A: Route kilometres divided by the number of trains
options.B: Train kilometres divided by the corresponding train hours
options.C: Net Tonne Kilometres divided by engine hours
options.D: Wagon kilometres divided by wagon days

e: Average speed of goods trains = train kilometres divided by the corresponding train hours.

q: Utilisation of coaching vehicles is measured by:

options.A: Vehicle kilometres per vehicle day
options.B: Passenger kilometres per train
options.C: Earnings per vehicle per year
options.D: The number of seats provided per coach

e: Utilisation of coaching vehicles is measured by vehicle kilometres per vehicle day, showing the average distance run daily by each vehicle.

q: The Freight Operations Information System (FOIS) primarily provides:

options.A: Reservation of passenger berths
options.B: Information relating to staff pay and allowances
options.C: Information for track maintenance planning
options.D: Real-time information on freight operations, including rake and wagon movements

e: FOIS primarily provides real-time information on freight operations, including rake and wagon movements, for planning and monitoring goods traffic.

q: The mobile application provided by Indian Railways for booking unreserved tickets is:

options.A: IRCTC Rail Connect
options.B: National Train Enquiry System
options.C: FOIS Mobile
options.D: UTS on Mobile

e: Unreserved tickets are booked on mobile phones through the 'UTS on Mobile' application.

q: Train-load (rake-load) class rates for goods traffic are applicable when:

options.A: Goods are booked in a single wagon only
options.B: The traffic is carried by a passenger train
options.C: A full rake load of traffic is offered for booking
options.D: The distance involved is less than 100 kilometres

e: Train-load (rake-load) class rates become applicable when a full rake load of traffic is offered for booking.

q: The freight rates and the rules relating to goods traffic are published in:

options.A: The Coaching Tariff
options.B: The Goods Tariff
options.C: The Works Manual
options.D: The Stores Code

e: Freight rates and the rules relating to goods traffic are published in the Goods Tariff.

q: Passenger fares and the rules relating to coaching traffic are published in:

options.A: The Goods Tariff
options.B: The Establishment Code
options.C: The Accounts Code
options.D: The Coaching Tariff

e: Passenger fares and the rules relating to coaching traffic are published in the Coaching Tariff.

q: The average lead of passenger traffic is computed as:

options.A: Passenger earnings divided by the number of passengers
options.B: Train kilometres divided by the number of passengers
options.C: Passenger kilometres divided by the number of passengers carried
options.D: Route kilometres divided by the number of trains

e: Average lead of passenger traffic = passenger kilometres divided by the number of passengers carried, giving the average distance travelled per passenger.

q: Earnings from suburban (local/EMU) passenger services form part of:

options.A: Goods earnings
options.B: Sundry other earnings
options.C: Capital receipts
options.D: Coaching earnings

e: Earnings from suburban (local/EMU) passenger services form part of coaching earnings.

q: Station earnings collected by a station are required to be remitted to the bank/cash office:

options.A: Daily
options.B: Weekly
options.C: Fortnightly
options.D: At the end of the month

e: Station earnings are required to be remitted to the bank or cash office daily, so that collections do not accumulate at the station.

q: Where a station remits an amount less than the earnings collected by it, the deficiency is:

options.A: Written off by the Station Master
options.B: Debited to the station and shown as outstanding against it
options.C: Adjusted against the earnings of the next station
options.D: Borne by the cash office

e: Where a station remits less than the earnings collected, the deficiency is debited to the station and shown as outstanding against it until made good.

q: A Blank Paper Ticket (BPT) is issued at a station when:

options.A: The passenger has lost his original ticket
options.B: The train by which the passenger wants to travel is cancelled
options.C: The printed card ticket for the required class and destination is not available in stock
options.D: The passenger is unable to pay the full fare

e: A Blank Paper Ticket is issued when the printed card ticket for the required class and destination is not available in the station's stock.

q: An Excess Fare Ticket (EFT) is issued:

options.A: By the booking clerk for issue of a duplicate ticket
options.B: By the parcel clerk for excess luggage
options.C: By the Station Master for refund of fare
options.D: By the ticket checking staff to a passenger found travelling without a proper ticket, on realisation of the fare due and the excess charge

e: An Excess Fare Ticket is issued by ticket checking staff to a passenger found travelling without a proper ticket, on realisation of the fare due and the excess charge.

q: A Ticket Deposit Receipt (TDR) is used where:

options.A: A passenger deposits money for booking a full train
options.B: Refund of fare is claimed in circumstances in which it cannot be granted across the counter and requires verification
options.C: A merchant deposits freight in advance
options.D: A season ticket is surrendered before expiry

e: A Ticket Deposit Receipt is used where refund of fare cannot be granted across the counter and requires verification before it is allowed.

q: Refunds of fares granted at a station are accounted for in the station accounts:

options.A: By deduction from the earnings of the station
options.B: As a separate item of expenditure of the station
options.C: Only at the close of the financial year
options.D: Through the salary bills of the station staff

e: Refunds of fares granted at a station are accounted for by deduction from the earnings of the station.

q: On cancellation of a reserved ticket, the amount refunded to the passenger is:

options.A: The full fare in every case
options.B: The fare plus the reservation charge
options.C: The fare after deduction of the prescribed cancellation charge
options.D: Half the fare in every case

e: On cancellation of a reserved ticket, the refund is the fare after deduction of the prescribed cancellation charge.

q: On cancellation of an e-ticket booked online, the refund amount (after charges) is:

options.A: Paid in cash at the station
options.B: Sent by cheque to the passenger
options.C: Adjusted against the passenger's next booking
options.D: Credited automatically to the bank account/card from which the payment was made

e: On cancellation of an e-ticket, the refund after charges is credited automatically to the bank account or card from which the payment was made.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Mail (postal) traffic on the Railways is carried under an arrangement with the Department of Posts.
2. The charges for carriage of mails are settled between the Railways and the Department of Posts through periodical billing/adjustment.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both are true: mail traffic is carried under an arrangement with the Department of Posts, and the carriage charges are settled between the Railways and the Postal Department through periodical billing and adjustment.

q: Traffic for the Armed Forces booked on military warrants/credit notes is treated as:

options.A: Credit traffic, the charges being recovered from the Defence authorities
options.B: Free traffic, no charges being leviable
options.C: Cash traffic paid by the individual soldiers
options.D: Traffic to be written off as a social service obligation

e: Traffic for the Armed Forces booked on military warrants or credit notes is credit traffic, the charges being recovered from the Defence authorities.

q: Parcels offered for carriage by rail are booked under a:

options.A: Railway Receipt
options.B: Parcel Way Bill
options.C: Goods Invoice
options.D: Luggage Ticket

e: Parcels offered for carriage are booked under a Parcel Way Bill, as distinct from goods, which are booked under a Railway Receipt.

q: In an 'assisted siding', as distinguished from a private siding:

options.A: The entire cost of the siding is borne by the siding owner
options.B: The entire cost of the siding is borne by the Railways
options.C: The cost of construction of the siding is shared between the Railways and the siding owner
options.D: The cost is borne by the State Government

e: In an assisted siding the cost of construction is shared between the Railways and the siding owner, unlike a private siding whose entire cost is borne by the owner.

q: In respect of a private siding, the charges for placement and removal of wagons and for shunting performed by railway locomotives are recovered from:

options.A: The consignor of the goods
options.B: The destination station
options.C: The State Government
options.D: The siding owner

e: In a private siding, charges for placement and removal of wagons and for shunting performed by railway locomotives are recovered from the siding owner.

q: Under Section 106 of the Railways Act, 1989, a claim for compensation for loss or damage to goods, or for refund of an overcharge, must be preferred in writing within:

options.A: Three months from the date of entrustment of the goods
options.B: Six months from the date of entrustment of the goods
options.C: One year from the date of entrustment of the goods
options.D: Two years from the date of entrustment of the goods

e: Under Section 106 of the Railways Act, 1989, a claim for compensation for loss or damage to goods, or for refund of an overcharge, must be preferred in writing within six months from the date of entrustment of the goods.

q: Claims for compensation for loss, damage or non-delivery of goods, and for refund of fares/freight, which are not settled by the railway administration, can be taken before the:

options.A: Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission only
options.B: Divisional Railway Manager
options.C: Railway Claims Tribunal
options.D: Comptroller and Auditor General

e: Claims for compensation and for refund of fares or freight which are not settled by the railway administration can be taken before the Railway Claims Tribunal.

q: The average number of wagons per goods train is computed as:

options.A: Goods wagon kilometres divided by goods train kilometres
options.B: Tonnes carried divided by the number of goods trains
options.C: Net Tonne Kilometres divided by train kilometres
options.D: Wagon days divided by train days

e: Average number of wagons per goods train = goods wagon kilometres divided by goods train kilometres.

q: The Operating Ratio of a railway represents:

options.A: Net revenue expressed as a percentage of the capital-at-charge
options.B: Working expenses expressed as a percentage of gross earnings
options.C: Goods earnings expressed as a percentage of total earnings
options.D: Capital expenditure expressed as a percentage of revenue expenditure

e: Operating Ratio = working expenses divided by gross earnings x 100; it shows the percentage of earnings absorbed by the working expenses of the railway.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Appropriations to the Depreciation Reserve Fund and the Pension Fund are treated as part of working expenses for computing the Operating Ratio.
2. The dividend payable to General Revenues is treated as part of working expenses for computing the Operating Ratio.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Statement 1 is true: appropriations to the Depreciation Reserve Fund and the Pension Fund form part of working expenses for the Operating Ratio. Statement 2 is false: dividend to General Revenues is paid out of surplus, not treated as a working expense.

q: An Operating Ratio of more than 100 indicates that:

options.A: The railway has earned a large surplus
options.B: The capital-at-charge has exceeded the block value
options.C: The dividend liability has been fully met
options.D: The working expenses of the railway exceed its gross earnings

e: An Operating Ratio of more than 100 means the working expenses of the railway exceed its gross earnings, leaving no surplus.

q: The load factor (occupation ratio) of coaching services is measured as:

options.A: Passenger earnings divided by the number of passengers
options.B: Train kilometres divided by coach kilometres
options.C: Passenger kilometres expressed in relation to the seat kilometres offered
options.D: Passengers carried divided by the number of trains run

e: The load factor of coaching services is passenger kilometres expressed in relation to the seat kilometres offered, showing how fully the capacity provided is occupied.

q: The ratio of Net Tonne Kilometres to Gross Tonne Kilometres indicates:

options.A: The proportion of the total load hauled which is revenue-earning (paying) load
options.B: The speed of goods trains
options.C: The density of traffic on the line
options.D: The proportion of empty wagons in the wagon fleet

e: The ratio of NTKM to GTKM indicates the proportion of the total load hauled which is revenue-earning (paying) load, the remainder being tare and non-paying load.

q: The 'percentage of engines under and awaiting repair' is an index of:

options.A: The repair position of locomotives and the efficiency of the locomotive maintenance organisation
options.B: Fuel efficiency of locomotives
options.C: Utilisation of wagons
options.D: Occupation of the line

e: The percentage of engines under and awaiting repair is an index of the repair position of locomotives and the efficiency of the locomotive maintenance organisation.

q: The compilation of railway statistics for Indian Railways as a whole is done in the Railway Board by the:

options.A: Accounts Directorate
options.B: Traffic (Commercial) Directorate
options.C: Finance (Budget) Directorate
options.D: Statistics and Economics Directorate

e: Compilation of railway statistics for Indian Railways as a whole is done in the Railway Board by the Statistics and Economics Directorate.

q: The 'passenger classification' statistics compiled on the Railways show:

options.A: The classification of trains as Mail, Express and Passenger
options.B: The classification of staff employed on passenger trains
options.C: The commodity classification of luggage traffic
options.D: The number of passengers booked and the earnings, class-wise

e: Passenger classification statistics show the number of passengers booked and the earnings therefrom, class-wise.

q: In goods traffic statistics, traffic is classified commodity-wise primarily in order to:

options.A: Fix the wages of goods shed staff
options.B: Decide the allotment of locomotives
options.C: Study the pattern and composition of goods traffic and its trends
options.D: Compute the wages of the operating staff

e: Goods traffic is classified commodity-wise primarily to study the pattern and composition of goods traffic and its trends over time.
